spreads.scene: One young woman, Maya, has just stepped into a long museum hall and stands small near the entrance, taking it in. The hall is grand and warm and hushed: honey wood floor, cream plaster walls, and along both walls a receding row of doors hung like paintings, each in a simple wooden frame with a soft spotlight from above and a low velvet rope on brass stanchions in front. The plaques beside the far doors are too small and too distant to read. Morning light falls from high windows. Keep the lower right of the frame calm and open floor.
spreads._caption: There is a hall where they keep the doors. Every company you have ever heard of walked in through one of them.

spreads.scene: A close, reverent study of one exhibited door in the hall: the plain honey-brown door hung flat on the cream museum wall in its simple wooden frame, a soft spotlight pooling on it from above, a low velvet rope on two brass stanchions in front. On the wall beside the frame, a small brass plaque with designed lettering that is fully legible and reads exactly "THE CLOUD", and nothing else. The frame, plaque, rope and light all sit beside or below the door and never touch its face. Keep the bottom right calm. The door leaf has EXACTLY FOUR recessed panels in TWO rows and no more: a top row of two small square panels, and below it a single row of two tall rectangular panels that reach nearly to the floor with only a plain flat rail beneath them. There is NO third row of panels at the bottom of the door.

a six-panel colonial door, a third row of panels at the bottom of the door leaf
spreads._caption: Each door has a frame, a spotlight, and a small brass plaque. Standing here, you would think nobody could have missed them.

spreads.scene: Two people fill the middle of the frame from the waist up: Gary, the guide, and Maya, the visitor, standing together in the museum hall. Gary is mid-sentence, turned toward Maya, one hand raised in a gentle explaining gesture; Maya listens with her head slightly tilted, genuinely weighing it. Behind them the row of framed, spotlit doors falls away soft and out of focus down the hall. Warm, unhurried light.
spreads._caption: The guide has walked this hall more times than he can count. He says the plaques are the part people get wrong. On the day it mattered, every door in this hall looked like this.

spreads.scene: Maya sits at a plain desk in a small evening room, calm, one mug beside her, her laptop open and unmistakably glowing warm Claude-orange: the screen light, a soft rim of orange light along the lid's edge, and the orange glow falling on her hands and the desk around it. Above and behind the screen the picture opens into the digital space, painted as a soft luminous workshop in the air: the Chief of Agents in its gold admiral hat stands nearest the screen receiving work, one sub-agent heads-down typing at a tiny holographic terminal, and one sub-agent mid-stride carrying a fanned armful of glowing papers toward the Chief with a thin dotted glowing tether arcing between them. Every agent stays inside the digital space; none crosses into the real room. Maya's real room stays quiet and warm and ordinary.
